summary: The Deaths in Custody Reporting Reform Act amends the Death in Custody Reporting Act of 2013 to enhance how deaths in federal and state custody are tracked, reported, and analyzed. It establishes detailed reporting requirements for law enforcement and correctional facilities, creates a review panel to examine reporting compliance, mandates studies and regular reporting by the National Institute of Justice and the Bureau of Justice Statistics, and requires the National Center for Health Statistics to update standard death certificates and provide access to the National Death Index. Additionally, it sets strict disclosure and investigation timelines for deaths occurring in immigration detention.

affected_groups.effect: Must collect and submit detailed quarterly reports regarding deaths in custody to the Bureau of Justice Statistics or the Bureau of Justice Assistance, face potential public hearings for reporting failures, and comply with subpoenas from the review panel.
affected_groups.group: Federal, state, and local law enforcement and correctional agencies

affected_groups.effect: Must provide notice of covered deaths within 48 hours, complete death reviews within 90 days, publish individual and joint annual reports, and maintain public websites detailing those deaths.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and U.S. Customs and Border Protection

affected_groups.effect: Tasked with compiling data, conducting studies, publishing annual reports, establishing consensus definitions, and maintaining public databases concerning deaths in custody.
affected_groups.group: Federal statistical and research agencies (Bureau of Justice Statistics, National Institute of Justice, National Center

affected_groups.effect: Gain access to a searchable public database of deaths in custody, open-source reporting tools, annual reports, and opportunities to submit testimony or information to the review panel.
affected_groups.group: General public, researchers, and families of individuals who died in custody

key_provisions: Expands requirements for reporting deaths in state and federal custody, including specific information on demographics, cause of death, location of the incident, and average daily populations.
Establishes a 6-member review panel appointed by the Attorney General to assess compliance, examine barriers to accurate reporting, hold public hearings, and issue recommendations.

Requires the Director of the Bureau of Justice Statistics to publish an annual report and maintain a searchable, publicly accessible online database of deaths in custody using official reports and open-source data.

Requires the National Institute of Justice to conduct periodic studies and submit reports to Congress regarding how custody-related deaths can be reduced and whether they relate to facility management.
Directs the National Center for Health Statistics to add a death-in-custody designation checkbox to the U.S. standard certificate of death and provide guidance to states to do the same.
Mandates that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and U.S. Customs and Border Protection disclose covered deaths within 48 hours and complete internal death investigations within 90 days.
Authorizes $6 million to be appropriated for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2037 to carry out sections 5 through 8 of the Act.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact mechanics or formulas for how states will have funds reallocated if they fail to comply, beyond permitting states to dedicate certain funds for compliance in the first fiscal year.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Deaths in Custody Reporting Reform Act amends the Death in Custody Reporting Act of 2013 to enhance how deaths in federal and state custody are tracked, reported, and analyzed. It establishes detailed reporting requirements for law enforcement and correctional facilities, creates a review panel to examine reporting compliance, mandates studies and regular reporting by the National Institute of Justice and the Bureau of Justice Statistics, and requires the National Center for Health Statistics to update standard death certificates and provide access to the National Death Index. Additionally, it sets strict disclosure and investigation timelines for deaths occurring in immigration detention.
summary_detail.significance: The bill broadens accountability and transparency regarding deaths occurring during interactions with law enforcement, inside correctional or juvenile facilities, and within immigration detention. By mandating rigorous public databases, independent reviews, standardized tracking on death certificates, and regular congressional reporting, the legislation substantially increases federal oversight and data collection surrounding mortality in custody.
